answer: Copying the same citations across 146 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 146 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the spiral index resolves every citation against the quartz checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the shale audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
